papers.title: Extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity in the hole-doped Hubbard model
papers.abstract: The two-dimensional Hubbard model was originally proposed as the minimal model of uniform $d$-wave superconductivity in the cuprate high-temperature superconductors, but recent calculations with relevant parameters in a realistic doping regime have often found other ground states. Further, uncertainty remains over such results due to the intrinsic bias of different computational methods. Here we address this uncertainty through state-of-the-art neural tensor network and neural backflow state simulations, enabled by large-scale GPU computation, that together reach an unprecedented variational accuracy on lattices with up to 1024 sites. At $1/8$ doping in the pure Hubbard model, as well as with next-nearest-neighbor hopping relevant to the hole-doped cuprates, we reveal a near degeneracy among a low-energy uniform $d$-wave state, superconducting stripes, and non-superconducting stripe states on the milli-$t$ energy scale. Our work rebalances the narrative that the Hubbard model supports a single dominant order in relevant parameter regimes towards a picture of extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity.

papers.title: Field-free superconducting diode and tunable vortex dynamics in NbN/FePt stripe-domain heterostructures
papers.abstract: We demonstrate reconfigurable, field-free superconducting diode behavior in NbN/FePt and NbN/AlN/FePt heterostructures with remanent stripe domains in the FePt layer. NbN films 10 nm thick are capped either directly with FePt or through a thin AlN spacer, which reduces electronic proximity effects while preserving magnetic coupling through stray fields. At zero applied magnetic field, the superconducting diode efficiency reaches approximately 50--60% in NbN/FePt when the stripes are perpendicular to the current and is strongly reduced when they are parallel. The diode effect persists in NbN/AlN/FePt with efficiencies reaching approximately 35--40%, supporting a magnetic origin of the nonreciprocity. We interpret the response as asymmetric vortex transport in the remanent magnetic landscape, with preferential edge vorticity and a Lorentz force that favors inward flux injection or outward motion depending on current polarity. Under applied perpendicular magnetic fields, the interplay between the external field and the magnetic stray fields modifies the flux-flow instability and the apparent instability velocity inferred from transport, with values below those reported for bare NbN films. These results show that stripe-domain ferromagnetic overlayers provide a reconfigurable route to control superconducting nonreciprocity and flux-flow stability in NbN-based heterostructures.

papers.title: Anisotropic thermoelectric transport in the Sr2RuO4-Ru eutectic system
papers.abstract: The Sr2RuO4-Ru eutectic system, in which metallic Ru inclusions are embedded in a Sr2RuO4 matrix, exhibits an enhanced superconducting onset temperature of about 3 K, known as the 3-K phase. Here we investigate the in-plane thermoelectric response of this eutectic system in the normal state and find a pronounced anisotropy in the thermopower for thermal gradients applied parallel and perpendicular to the Ru lamellae. To clarify its origin, we combine thermopower measurements with electronic-structure-based transport calculations and finite-element modeling of the local strain distribution generated by the thermal-expansion mismatch between Sr2RuO4 and Ru. The calculations show that uniaxial compression of Sr2RuO4 produces a sizable thermopower anisotropy through modification of the Fermi surfaces. When an idealized spatially inhomogeneous strain field around the Ru lamellae is included, the observed sign and qualitative magnitude of the anisotropy are reproduced more closely than in a simple unstrained two-component model. These results are consistent with a substantial contribution from strain-induced changes in the Sr2RuO4 electronic structure near the interfaces, although contributions from interfacial phase mixing and three-dimensional transport connectivity cannot be excluded.

papers.title: Cluster property and entanglement in the superconducting state
papers.abstract: We present the conditions for satisfying the cluster property in the superconducting state. Using these conditions, we show that the cluster property employed when deriving the order parameter of the superconducting state (OPSS) holds true, and that the OPSS is given by ${}_S\langle \Psi | \hat{\psi}(x)\hat{\psi}(x') | \Psi \rangle_S$, where $|\Psi\rangle_S$ is the superconducting state, and where $\hat{\psi}(x)$ is the field operator of superconducting electrons. This provides a resolution to the long-standing concern raised by Leggett et al.\ regarding particle-number fluctuation in the superconducting state. In addition, by considering the entanglement between two particles composed of the maximum geminal of the BCS ground state [J.\ Phys. Commun. 5, 095003 (2021)], it is confirmed that the larger the deviation from the conditions for satisfying the cluster property becomes, the greater the magnitude of the entanglement becomes. This shows not only the effectiveness of the conditions for satisfying the cluster property but also the justification of the OPSS that has been commonly used.

papers.title: Coulomb-Driven Electronic Textures in Lightly Hole-Doped Cuprates
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent experiments on Ca$_2$CuO$_2$Cl$_2$, we present a comprehensive study of the interplay between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets in lightly hole-doped cuprates. Owing to the poorly screened Coulomb potential, the interactions between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets favor asymmetric electronic configurations characterized by effective electric "dipoles". Using the MPS-based Lanczos method, we show that these localized holes give rise to in-gap bound states within the charge-transfer gap. When tunneling matrix-element effects are included, the bound states exhibit a characteristic $4a_0 \times 2a_0$ internal structure, consistent with experimental observations. Our results suggest that Coulomb interactions between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets, together with tunneling matrix-element effects, provide a microscopic mechanism for the observed $4a_0$ electronic structures.

papers.title: Contact Renormalization of One-Mode Electron Correlation: Validation in Four- and Ten-Electron Systems
papers.abstract: A stationary many-electron eigenstate has one dynamical phase although its internal response can be strongly multimode. We ask whether the stationary Hartree--Fock information carrier contains enough information to determine the scalar correlation energy through one effective return. In regularized Hartree--Fock, Gaussian primitive products fix a minimum-information relative-coordinate mode before any one-mode reduction; virial completion defines the correlation source, while exact contact measures the additional return restriction created by neighboring occupied pairs. The Be-like $1s^22s^2$ sequence establishes the one-valence-pair boundary: with no neighboring occupied valence pair, the source returns through the universal floor $D_0=\sqrt{1+\delta^2}$. Ten-electron molecules and Ne-like ions then test how finite-pair contact dresses that return. The same parameter-free source--return construction reproduces the established molecular and ionic correlation trends with quantitative accuracy. The numerical agreement therefore serves as validation of a physical separation between source strength and return restriction, rather than as the objective by itself.

papers.title: Extended strange metal and superconductivity in partially filled moir\'e Hubbard bands
papers.abstract: Moir\'e semiconductors provide a physical realization of the Hubbard model. Bandwidth-tuned Mott transitions and complex phase diagrams mimicking those of high-temperature superconductors have been demonstrated near a weak Mott insulating state at half-band-filling. The platform also provides an opportunity to explore the physics of a partially filled Hubbard band at doping densities far away from the Mott insulator, a regime that has remained largely unexplored. Here we report the emergence of an extended strange metal (ESM), in both doping density and twist angle, in a partially filled Hubbard band of twisted bilayer WSe2. The ESM is in the clean limit, persists down to about 50mK, and spans over multiple symmetry-breaking ground states; it also appears only at small twist angles, where electronic correlations are strong. These observations distinguish the state from the reported strange metals associated with quantum criticality and favor the viewpoint that it is an intrinsic state of matter. We also report the observation of a new superconducting dome being developed from the ESM but far away from both the Mott insulating state and the van Hove singularity of the material. Our work opens the door to exploring the new regime of partially filled Hubbard bands in the clean limit.

papers.title: Benchmarking the accuracy of superconducting pair-pair correlations within Constrained Path Quantum Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Ground state properties of the Hubbard model are of fundamental importance to understand the mechanism of unconventional superconductivity in the high-T_c cuprates and other materials. One of the most powerful numerical methods for strongly interacting models is quantum Monte Carlo, which however faces a fundamental limitation, the Fermion sign problem. The sign problem can be mitigated using approximate methods such as Constrained Path Monte Carlo, where the sign of the overlap with a trial wavefunction is constrained to remain positive. Beyond the constraint, additional approximations must be made in order to measure observables for operators that do not commute with the Hamiltonian. We examine critically the most commonly used approximation, back propagation, as well as a recently proposed constraint release measurement technique. In comparisons with a variety of systems that can be solved numerically exactly by other methods, we find that back propagation tends to underestimate long-range superconducting pair-pair correlations. Except in special cases such as one dimension, back propagation introduces an uncontrolled approximation even when the exact trial wavefunction is used. The constraint release technique can provide accurate results, with the disadvantages that it much more computationally expensive and reintroduces the sign problem.

papers.title: Slave-boson Formalism for Superconducting Pairing at Strong Coupling
papers.abstract: We study the emergence of superconductivity in the one-band Hubbard model using the spin-rotation-invariant Kotliar-Ruckenstein slave-boson (SB) approach. Motivated by its intrinsically renormalized mean-field ground state, we construct an effective pairing vertex from dynamical fluctuations about the saddle point. Solving the anisotropic, frequency-dependent gap equation on the square lattice, we map the pairing instabilities across doping, interaction, temperature and real-frequency gap structure that qualitatively match experimental cuprate observations. This framework merges strong-correlation SB-type renormalizations with RPA-type pairing transparency, providing a scalable route to modeling multi-orbital superconductivity at strong coupling.

papers.title: Superheating field of clean superconductors near the type-I--type-II boundary: the low-temperature Meissner stability limit of niobium
papers.abstract: We calculate the low-temperature superheating field $B_{\rm sh}$ of clean superconductors near the boundary between type-I and type-II superconductivity, with particular emphasis on Nb. Ginzburg--Landau theory is not applicable at low temperatures, while previous microscopic calculations have been limited to either the large-$\kappa$ regime or the dirty limit. The clean, low-$\kappa$ regime relevant to Nb has therefore remained unresolved. We solve the self-consistent nonlinear nonlocal Eilenberger problem for the Meissner state and then analyze its stability against small perturbations. For a Nb-like material with $\kappa_{\rm GL}=0.7$, we obtain $B_{\rm sh}\simeq 290\,{\rm mT}$ at $T/T_c=0.2$, using $B_{c0}\simeq 200\,{\rm mT}$. For a TESLA-shaped Nb accelerator cavity, this corresponds to an intrinsic Meissner-stability limit of about $67\,{\rm MV/m}$.

papers.title: Nontrivial Boundary-Mediated Superconducting Transport in a TRSB Topological Iron-Based Superconductor
papers.abstract: The interplay of superconductivity, band topology, and spontaneous time-reversal-symmetry breaking (TRSB) is expected to enable topological superconducting boundary states. FeTe0.55Se0.45 provides a promising single-material platform because it combines superconductivity, nontrivial band topology, and spontaneous magnetization in the superconducting state. Here we report evidence for a boundary-mediated superconducting transport response in exfoliated Fe(Te,Se) devices. Polar Kerr measurements show that TRSB emerges below TKerr < Tc and coexists with superconductivity across multiple compositions, providing an independent symmetry-breaking scale for transport. Using crystallographically sharp, continuous edges and side-surface-dominant contacts, we find that topological FeTe0.55Se0.45 exhibits an anomalous conductance plateau absent in topologically trivial FeTe0.40Se0.60 and Fe1.02Te0.55Se0.45 under comparable measurements. This plateau requires uninterrupted sharp edges connecting source and drain, persists over micrometer-scale separations far exceeding the bulk coherence length, shows strongly suppressed thermal broadening, and collapses when the drain is moved to the top surface. Its temperature evolution follows the TRSB scale: the plateau remains weakly broadened below T*Kerr and disappears near TKerr rather than Tc. These doping-selective, edge-geometry-dependent, TRSB-correlated, and long-range nonlocal signatures establish experimental criteria for identifying boundary-mediated superconducting transport in FeTe0.55Se0.45 and motivate phase-sensitive and theoretical studies of its microscopic origin.

papers.title: Microscopic theory of the lower critical field in superconducting thin-film strips
papers.abstract: The lower critical field $B_{c1}$ of a narrow superconducting thin-film strip sets the thermodynamic scale for vortex-free operation in a perpendicular magnetic field. The standard Pearl--London estimate requires a phenomenological vortex-core cutoff, because the London theory does not resolve the core. We formulate a microscopic theory for a dirty strip by solving the two-dimensional Usadel equations in the film plane, with the applied field included directly in the gauge-invariant momentum. Self-consistent vortex and Meissner solutions are computed at fixed field, and $B_{c1}$ is obtained from their Gibbs-energy difference. The calculation resolves the vortex core and its finite-width deformation without introducing a cutoff. The resulting vortex self-energy is larger than the naive Pearl--London estimate and cannot, in general, be represented by a London logarithm with a single width-independent cutoff. The formulation applies at any $T<T_c$ and provides a microscopic basis for predicting $B_{c1}$ in superconducting nanostrips and related thin-film devices.

papers.title: What Becomes of the Antiferromagnetic String When Long Range Neel Order Is Lost? Exact Results
papers.abstract: Early string descriptions of doped antiferromagnets associate hole motion in a locally N\'eel-ordered background with a path-dependent antiferromagnetic string. We ask what becomes of this mechanism when long range N\'eel order is lost while short range antiferromagnetic correlations persist. In a singlet bond representation, the underlying basis states do not assign an oriented \(A/B\) spin registration to each bond. Therefore, any surviving long wavelength antiferromagnetic axis is naturally described as a director, \(\mathbf n\sim-\mathbf n\). Long range N\'eel order can nevertheless provide a global \(S^2\) lift of this director field; when that long range registration is lost, non liftable configurations of the \(RP^2\) manifold become physically accessible, opening a topologically nontrivial \(\mathbb Z_2\) sector. Its elementary defects are half vortices that globally minimize the \(RP^2\) \(\sigma\)-model energy within the nontrivial \(\mathbb Z_2\) sector. An \textit{a posteriori} energetic comparison further shows that the projective half vortex texture is softer than the corresponding vector reference texture. A pair of half vortices with opposite windings is logarithmically confined, \(V(R) = \kappa \ln\left(R/r_{\text{core}}\right)\), \(\kappa = \pi \rho_s /2\). The resulting confinement is carried not by a one dimensional string but by an extended two-dimensional spin texture. Thus, the loss of long-range N\'eel order does not eliminate antiferromagnetic confinement but removes the global N\'eel lift. This activates a distinct projective mechanism in which a local path dependent string is replaced, at long wavelengths, by a global topological texture with logarithmic confinement.
